title: Pilot implementation of wearable technology (chest monitor) in nursing care at the University Hospital Bonn.
summary: This study aims to evaluate the application and benefits of wireless technology for measuring vital signs such as blood pressure and pulse in nursing care on general hospital wards. Wearables are small technical devices worn on the body that can collect externally measurable bodily functions using various technologies. The chest monitor used in this study features a sensor capable of determining measurements via infrared light (PPG signal) from the blood vessels directly beneath the skin. The chest monitor measures blood pressure, pulse, oxygen saturation, and body temperature. We want to investigate whether the device can replace manual vital sign measurement, whether sleep quality improves due to the elimination of nighttime awakenings for measurement, and whether we can detect the onset of, for example, an infection with fever earlier if needed. The wearable is attached to the chest with an adhesive patch. For showering or examinations, the monitor is unclipped from the patch, and the patch is removed. A patch change can occur at any time. To understand how wearing the wearable is perceived and whether the expected goals are being met, we will distribute a questionnaire to patients and nursing staff and interview nurses from the wards.
conditions: This study does not focus on specific illnesses or conditions. It is a procedural investigation of nursing workflows on hospital wards, aimed at determining how to improve patients’ sleep hygiene and increase feelings of security through the implementation of technology.

interventions.name: Implementation of a wearable (chest monitor) for wireless measurement of vital signs on general wards as a replacement for manual vital sign measurements, for example, at night to improve sleep hygiene. The wearable is worn for varying durations depending on the length of the patient’s hospital stay

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Adult patients admitted to the hospital who are capable of giving informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
Patients requiring continuous monitoring, Tattoos in the chest area, Allergies to metals, plastic, silicone, or adhesive bandage materials, Excessive patient movement
Methaemoglobin in the blood, Intravascular dyes, Regular proximity to devices emitting high levels of harmful interference (including portable and mobile RF communication devices such as CT, MRI, diathermy, RFID, and electronic article surveillance systems)
Significant deformities, swelling, irritation, wounds, degenerative changes, or edema in the chest area
